Comments: On April 9 2026, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the Ackerman 2 OG Well. This well is under Consent Order and Agreement (COA) 407094. The well was reportedly plugged on 2/27/2025, therefore the site shall be restored no later than 11/27/2025.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department was unable to locate a restoration plan onsite. Therefore, the Department was unable to compare the well site to the restoration plan, however, the Department was able to assess the access road and well site for permanent stabilization and vegetative growth.Upon inspection of the access road, it appeared to have achieved 70% uniform and adequate vegetative coverage. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed at the time of the inspection.Upon inspection of the former well site, the Department observed an above ground monument for the reportedly plugged well. No other production equipment was observed on site. There were no observed leaks at the surface in the area surrounding the well monument. The well site did not appear to have achieved 70% uniform and adequate vegetative coverage (photo 4). The Department did not observe any erosion and sedimentation controls installed on site. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed at the time of the inspection.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to have E and S controls installed as well as failure to have an E and S plan onsite.

Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of less than 20 gallons of antifreeze. The release was reported by Peg Farrell, Chief, at 14:43 on 11/26/19. The release was reportedly due to human error. A compressor had been disconnected and pulled aside when a valve was opened allowing the antifreeze to leak from the GPUs onsite. When I arrived, I spoke with Greg, Chief, and we observed the impacted area. They had excavated about 12 cubic yards of pad material and placed it in a container. The area was about to be back-filled with fresh gravel. During this inspection, no other impacts were noted beyond the excavated area. Based on Chief's response to the release, the results of this inspection is Violations Immediately Corrected.

Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days.
Violation ID: 972184
Permit API: 063-31807
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana
Municipality: Grant Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 10/17/2022
Comments: EPA Mechanical Integrity Test was conducted on 10/12/2022 at 09:58. Tubing pressure at commencement of test was 2225 p.s.i. Tubing annulus was filled with freshwater and pressured up to 800 p.s.i. MIT concluded at 10:28. Final pressure on tubing annuls was 800 p.s.i. Final pressure on tubing was 2225 p.s.i. Annulus of surface casing was monitored while the pressure test was underway, for any changes in the rate of bubbling. There were no abnormalities observed, indicating there is zonal isolation between the downhole injection zone, and the top-hole freshwater protection zones. The well has passed EPA's mechanical integrity test. PGE's remediation plan proposes the use of a resin material, with gas blocking capabilities. The resin will be pumped into the annular space of the surface casing at a depth of approximately 350', or the cap rock nearest this depth. This depth is determined to be below the deepest fresh groundwater in the area. It is anticipated that by placing the resin at this depth, the cap rock will be restored, thereby preventing the gas from permeating the micro-annulus that is allowing the gas to flow to surface. The resin has been used in similar annular gas scenarios, with success. An alternative procedure of pumping cement into the annular space has been discussed, but the outcome of this procedure is often times unpredictable, and could leave the casing integrity in a compromised condition. PGE anticipates that the resin will be available to them in April, of 2023. The product is currently in short supply, and the available stock has been allotted to other customers.

Violation ID: 8153366
Permit API: 121-45433
Unconventional: No
County: Venango

Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/21/2023
Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023.There is an active discharge of fluid from the Tank Battery of the Lower Reno oil lease that is permitted and operated by Petro Erie Inc.. The public water supply for the town of Reno, PA is under a "Do Not Consume Advisory" based upon an increase in TDS for the Bellows Spring Cistern (owned and operated by Venango Water Company).The tank battery consists of (2) 210bbl steel tanks and (4) 100bbl poly tanks. The earthen dike appears to be lined with a plastic liner. There is a dike drain that is located in the southwest corner of the dike. The valve on the drain pipe is open and fluid is flowing to the ground. The area inside the dike appears to have been impacted by produced fluid from the tanks. A pipeline between two of the poly tanks was actively dripping fluid. Field screening inside the dike were conducted with the soil probe for conductivity, and all readings were above the range of the meter (20,000uS).The discharge from the dike drain flows south across an open area and into a wooded area. There is a visible impact area extending from the dike drain in an irregular pattern approximately 80 yards from the earthen dike and approximately ranging from 6' to 25' in width. Field screening within the impacted area was conducted approximately every 10 yards. Conductivity measurements ranged from 11,000uS to above the range of the meter (20,000uS). Several areas outside of the impacted area were checked with the soil probe and the levels ranged between 60uS to 164uS. An oil sheen is visible within the flowing water and dead vegetation is also observed including several large cherry trees within the impacted area. The amount of discharged fluid is unknown and based upon the observations onsite it appears that the discharge has been occurring for some time.The dike drain was closed by DEP staff at 8:45am to stop the continued discharge of fluid outside of the earthen dike.Water samples were collected at the dike drain outlet (discharge point) and sent to the lab for analysis. Water samples were also collected at the Bellows Spring Cistern (41.422360 -79.764490) which is a source for a public water supply of the town of Reno, PA.While onsite the Department talked with the operator/owner (Harry Rhoades) via a phone conversation. The discharge and the potential that the discharge may be impacting the public water supply was discussed with Mr. Rhoades. Mr. Rhoades insisted that he does not discharge his brine and that he could provide disposal documents. It was stated that the dike drain was left open because of forecasted rain. Violations are cited.The Oil and Gas Inspector (OGI) will be conducting a separate well compliance inspection for the well and other wells on the lease.

Comments: On 5/06/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection in response to a complaint (CTS-397312) at the Clara Jacques 1 well plugging site in Wharton Township, Fayette County. This inspection also follows-up to IR 4186065, where violations were issued against severe tire rutting observed in the access road.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) was entered into between the Department and Diversified on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified is to restore the Well Site after in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S.A. 3216; after completion of plugging operations.The following was observed during the inspection:A Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is installed at the site entrance along Five Forks Road (photos 1 and 2). An additional RCE is installed where the access road meets the well site, in accordance with the E and S plan drawing. The RCE adjacent to the well plugging site is laden with sediment (photos 15 and 22). Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is installed on site in the locations shown on E and S plan drawing (photos 9, 12, 17, 19, and 20). Significant tire rutting remains throughout the access road. Due to the soft and damp soil conditions that appear to exist on site, the Department recommended in IR 4186065 that the operator consider additional E and S control measures as necessary, to prevent accelerated erosion and sedimentation from occurring on site. Well plugging equipment was observed on site, however plugging operations do not appear to be occurring at the time of inspection. A puddle with swirly rainbow sheen was observed adjacent to well plugging rig. This swirly rainbow sheen remained intact when disturbed, which is a known indicator of a petroleum-based release.The Department identified an access road cross-culvert at the time of IR 4186065 (photo 23). No loose sediment was observed in the cross-culvert during this inspection. However, the Department recommended in IR 4186065 that the operator take necessary measures to ensure that the cross-culvert is protected from sedimentation.Based on observations from this inspection, violations issued in IR 4186065 shall remain outstanding. Additional violations shall be issued for failure to adequately protect the cross-culvert shown in Photo 14 and for failure maintain the RCE adjacent to the well plugging site. Additional volations may be forthcoming against the swirly rainbow sheen released adjacent to the well plugging rig.

Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that on Sunday, January 23, 2022 at 1345 a well operator observed a dump line attached to a GPU on the pad that was dripping liquid. The operator estimated that 5-10 gallons of produced water was released. In a follow-up email sent by Regina Logue of Rockdale on the same day, she stated that the fluid was vacuumed up and a foot-deep hole was excavated. The site is snow-covered. Two wells are staged for production on the pad. Two GPUs are present without secondary containment. I observed that next to the GPUs, a small hole has been dug beneath a valve. A Repsol representative arrived on location and confirmed that the release had occurred from this valve and the small hole beneath it on the pad surface was where excavation had taken place. The Repsol representative stated that the release occurred while a well tender was inside the GPU so the individual was able to stop the release immediately. No puddles, slush, or stains can be observed anywhere on the pad. The excavated hole had snow in it as well. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.

Comments: On 11/21/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alterations inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 36 degrees and partly cloudy when I arrived on location. Rainfall had impacted the region in the past 24 hours.Inspecting the original Taft 851 1V pad, I did witness a secondary containment structure containing drilling mats with water at the level of the containment wall and fluid from the containment on the unprotected ground (picture 5). The water field tested at 0.301 mS conductance. Seneca's Jeff Passerrello was notified and was scheduling to have the containment emptied.Anthony Murphy described current operations as follows: A Nextier frac fleet has finished completion operations on five new wells at the site. Two snubbing/well servicing units were on site, drilling plugs out of the five completed wells. The units were on the first two wells and Anthony expects it to take a week to drill plugs on each well. He expects the crews to finish drilling plugs on all five wells by 12/10/2024. Anthony accompanied me on the site inspection. All operations were being conducted within a plastic lined containment structure that was protected by drilling mats. I did witness frac tanks, gas buster tanks, vac boxes and various chemical totes staged in secondary containment. There were ten frac tanks with fresh and produced water, six gas busters, and eight vac boxes staged near the snubbing/servicing units all staged in secondary containment. 28 frac tanks were staged in secondary containment on the west side of the location. I did witness water in the transfer manifold duck pond on the west side of the snubbing units that field tested at 19.99 mS conductance. Anthony will have the liquids removed.During the inspection, I did witness a 5' x 8' water puddle near the north-central pad outfall that field tested at 19.99 mS conductance; I collected water sample 9551-145. The upper conductivity limit of the Oakton PCTS5 is 19.99 mS. Water discharging from the north-central pad outfall into the sediment basin field tested at 19.99 mS conductance; I collected water sample 9551-146 and soil sample 9551-147. Water in the basin near the northeast overflow field tested at 3.07 mS conductance; I collected water sample 9551-148. Vegetation is established in recently constructed areas. Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Infiltration berm 3 and the sedimentation basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations. As recommended in the inspections listed above, the DEP continues to recommend pursuing Act 2 for the large amount of elevated conductance fluids discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin.The DEP recommends the following: 1. Remove the elevated conductance fluids and contaminated soils from the pad surface and the sediment basin.2. Continuously monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered.3. Monitor secondary containment structures for contaminants, for liquid levels and for adequate freeboard levels; remove liquids as necessary.I left the site at 1300 hours.

Comments: Incident inspection of Expand's "Lucy" Marcellus well site.Steve Moyer (Expand) called the DEP on September 18, 2025 (yesterday) to report an unknown quantity of brine released onto the pad surface that they discovered the same day.I met with Steve Moyer on site. Expand finished hydraulically fracturing the 6 new Marcellus wells at this site. He explained that while washing wooden mats yesterday on top of plastic liner they discovered a hole in the liner which leaked some of the wash water onto the pad surface. After removing the liner a vac truck removed pooled liquid from the pad surface. Then an excavator that was already on site to grade the pad removed the moist pad material in the approximately 50'x160' area and 1-2" deep. That material is now staged on felt and plastic liners and covered with plastic liner on the NW corner of the pad. Expand completed the cleanup the same day of the release. Crescent Environmental directed the cleanup and field verified it by testing electrical conductivity (EC) of the pad material. The impacted pad material had EC of 5-6 mS/cm. They also collected confirmatory samples of the material after the cleanup was complete. Chesapeake spudded 6 conductor casings here on October 9, 2024. Comments: On 03/11/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainees Olivia Holley, Madison Raviart, and Christina Mauri (PA DEP).On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). The following was observed:Some stabilization was used along the upper portion of the access road. Several areas throughout the entire access road did not have stabilization on the open soils. I recommend that stabilization is applied (Photos 1-4). Some areas had vegetation establishing (Photos 2, 4, 5).The channel that runs along the access road did not have rip rap or stabilization. Accelerated erosion and sediment accumulation were noted within this channel, which leads to several culverts along the road (Photo 6).The upper culvert, located at 40.113707 -79.966213, had sediment accumulation within the collection point. I recommend that this is addressed (Photo 7). The culvert located at 40.11300, -79.96751 had large amounts of sediment accumulated within the collection point. The culvert was not able to be seen due to the large amount of sediment within this area (Photos 8, 9). Accelerated erosion was noted within the accumulated sediment (Photo 9). The outlet point of this culvert was covered by the roads gravel/dirt, which was causing accelerated erosion and sediment transport towards the vegetation (Photos 10-12). I recommend that this is addressed. The culvert leading to the collection box was not functioning. Sediment was accumulated and an entry point into the pipe was approximately 99% covered. Accelerated erosion and sedimentation throughout the area and vegetation were noted leading from the channel towards the collection box. There was some sediment laden water within this box. This outlets into the vegetation, where sediment accumulation was noted. The vegetation was accumulating water, which leads towards the stream within the wood line (Photos 13-19). The lower culvert outlets into a channel. Sediment accumulation was noted within the channel. I recommend that rip rap is used within this channel, as this leads directly to the stream (Photos 20, 21).The culverts along the first portion of the access road, near the site gate, were not cleaned out. Potholes along the road were not addressed. Channelization was noted leading from the potholes off of the road. The beginning of the access road, where it meets the township road, was not addressed. This area was previously displaying high levels of flow, leading onto the township road, and depositing sediment. This was noted within IR 3701625, photos 24 and 15 (Photos 22-25). The violations issued on 01/24/2024, IR 3701625, remain outstanding.

Comments: This inspection is taking place in response to an operator reported spill. The incident was reported to the Department at approximately 6:33PM on 12/23/2020. Mr. Hardy from EQT was spoken to by phone on 12/24/2020. According to Mr. Hardy, the incident occurred at approximately 4:30PM on 12/23/2020. According to Mr. Hardy a pipe inside the GPU housing leaked, with approximately 5-10 gallons of fluid impacting the ground. The operator contacted SPSI to remediate. According to an email received from Mr. Hardy later in the day, impacted water was seeping from underneath the GPU into an excavated ditch. The operator has left the ditch open to act as a sump and the water will be vacuumed out as necessary. Per the operator, remediation is being conducted in accordance with 78a.66c(1), in reference to spills or releases less than 42 gallons. Based on that, the Department recommends that the operator fully remediate the site in accordance with 91.33(B), otherwise the Department requests that the operator reevaluate how much fluid was lost. Pictures taken by the operator have been attached to this inspection (Photo 1-6). Based on this inspection, violations are being issued for the discharge to the ground. The Department will schedule an on-site visit to follow up with the remediation effort as soon as possible. Pending the operator's response and the follow up inspection, further violations may be issued.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-06-18
Comments: Follow-up inspection conducted to assess overall site conditions on and off the pad. I was accompanied by Sasha Minium, DEP WQS Supervisor for this inspection. Heavy rain within the hours preceding this inspection caused there to be a large amount of water sitting on the pad surface, flowing from the PVC pipe to the west of the pad, and in the wetland and Salt Spring Run to the west of the pad. The 2H and 4H wells are still in flowback. Conductivity readings near the MASS were below 0.8 mS/cm. Taylor Parsons of Falcon accompanied us while we screened the pad surface for conductivity. Conductivities on the pad surface were less than 500 mS/cm. A vacuum truck was on location during the inspection removing water from the pad surface. A work crew was in the process of attaching plumbing from the well heads to the production equipment. A water sample and a conductivity reading was taken from each monitoring point with the exception of SW-6, the wetland near Salt Spring Run, and SW-7, the confluence of the wetland and Salt Spring Run, due to the high volume of water in Salt Spring Run and the wetland and due to the swift current in Salt Spring Run. Outstanding violations.

No issues noted on Pad B.On Pad A, Rick Hall showed me where the drilling mud release occurred. The pad surface had already been scraped by the time of this inspection. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/11/2025 to BLACKHILL ENERGY LLC in Springfield Township, Bradford county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BLACKHILL ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/11/2025
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8224484
Permit API: 015-23931
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Springfield Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/11/2025
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Blackhill Energy's Black Sam Bellamy Well Site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 3/11/2025 at 1420 hours. The weather was 68 degrees F with clear skies. An Act 9 sign, site plans and operator inspection log are located near the site entrance. The four Marcellus wells onsite remain under flowback conditions. Silt sock remains in place as necessary to prevent potential sedimentation from escaping the site's limit-of-disturbance. Three managed release concept (MRC) basins remain in place for the site's post-construction stormwater management. No evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed escaping the site. Gas production units, temporary storage tanks and production tanks are all held within secondary containment.During the inspection, pooled fluids on the pad surface behind the temporary storage tanks were field measured for electrical conductivity utilizing an Oakton PCTS 50 meter. The pooled fluids returned readings ranging from ~1.8 to 5.45mS/cm. Pooled fluids field measured can be seen in photos #9 and 10. Based on the elevated EC fluids located outside of secondary containment, I collected a sample for standard analysis code 942 from the fluid field measured at ~5.45mS/cm, shown in photo #11. Sample #0983-469 can be seen in photos #12 and 13 next to the sample location.Based on the discovery of elevated EC fluids located outside of secondary containment, a violation of CSL 402(b) [35 P.S. 691.402(b)] is cited against API #015-23931 at this time. Additional violations may be cited based on the analytical results from sample #0983-469. These findings were reported to Blackhill Energy via phone. Blackhill Energy had a crew dispatched the evening of 3/11/2025 to recover fluids on the pad surface and to scrape some pad material in the potentially impacted areas.The DEP recommends the following:-continuing elevated EC fluid and pad material recovery as necessary-placing the "ethylene glycol-water" storage tanks within secondary containment-recovering elevated EC fluids held within the temporary storage tanks' secondary containmentI departed the site at 1600 hours.

Comments: This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack that appears to have been recently produced. A sticker is posted on the pump jack displaying the operator's information, the well's API number is written on the jack. There was no activity onsite during this inspection. An approximate 2' x 5' area of vegetation and soil are stained with a coating of crude oil on the well site from the apparent repeated venting of this well into the atmosphere. The same practice is prevalent at a majority of the well sites on the Warrant 2980 lease and will be addressed in a separate inspection report. A tank battery that is located approximately 250' southeast of well consists of four steel and six plastic storage tanks inside of an earthen diking. There are several areas of stained gravel near the tanks (and at a compressor that is also located inside of the diking) which is indicative of production fluid releases onto the gravel inside of the containment.The exterior (southern) wall of the diking is void of vegetation and the specific conductance (SPC) is elevated (3800 uS/cm per field meter). It appears that the production fluid that has been released into the gravel inside of the tank battery diking has migrated through the southern wall of the containment and into a roadside ditch that flows south towards a cross culvert approximately 200 feet south of the well. BMPs (ditches and cross culverts) that are installed along these roads are not functioning properly, as a result, accelerated erosion is occurring over various stretches of the road surface. Additional E and S concerns on this lease are documented in the 5/11/23 inspection report for 053-29536 (Warrant 2980 #37).It is requested that documentation of production water disposal from this lease be provided to the Department. Please see the attached Notice of Violation regarding requested information pertaining to the cause of the release and intentions to remediate the contaminated material within and outside of the tank battery.

Comments: On May 27, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Chabal 2 well site in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3972746 where violations issued from IR 3965337 were left outstanding. During the time of IR 3972746, excavation and remediation work had started onsite but did not yet appear to be complete. Two covered excavation stockpile was observed onsite, however the impacted area appeared to remain adequately protected to mitigate risk of the impact being spread by stormwater.On the day of this inspection prior to arriving onsite, the Department spoke via phone with Penneco representative Marc Jacobs who explained that all material that was impacted by the 4/24/2025 crude oil and brine release has been excavated and awaits transport from site. Subsequent backfill and seeding of the formerly impacted area and screening underneath the brine tank location in response to observations made in Photos 9 and 10 of IR 3967072 are to follow.The following was observed:The well head is equipped with a well tag appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photo 2). The operator's information is posted on the separator (see photo 3). The body of the brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection (see photo 4). The covered excavation stockpiles that were observed onsite during the time IR 3972746 remain (see photos 5, 6, and 10). It appears that additional excavation was conducted on the formerly impacted area since the time of IR 3972746. It remains covered with plastic sheeting (see photos 7-9). Oil absorbent booms remain placed downslope of the covered impacted area (see photo 10). No evidence of visual impacts and/or elevated conductivity were detected downslope of impacted area (see photos 11 and 12).Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that remedial excavation has been completed and the impacted soil stockpiles remain adequately protected to mitigate risk of the impact being spread by stormwater until they are transported from site for disposal.Violations issued from IR 3965337 shall remain outstanding, as an NOI to Remediate and/or Final Report has not yet been submitted to the Department's ECB for review.

Comments: This administrative inspection documents the receipt of sample results for samples taken on the pad on 4/17/19 and samples taken in the sediment ditch (background and where fluid from the pad entered) and sediment trap outfall taken on 4/18/19. The sample from the pad (ID #0939078) shows elevated levels of barium and strontium, and while the chloride result was cancelled, these elevated parameters show that the high conductance fluid on the pad was likely a release produced water or flowback. The elevated chlorides, barium, and strontium in sample ID #0939080 (as compared to background, represented by sample ID #0939079) show that the fluid migrated from the pad, into the ditch, and into the sediment trap. Sample ID #0939081 taken from the sediment trap outfall shows higher levels of barium, strontium, and chlorides than the sediment ditch background sample, demonstrating that the fluid was released from the sediment trap. The failure to report a release of a regulated substance to the ground is a violation of 25 PA Code 78a.66(b). The release of the fluid to the pad surface is a violation of 25 PA Code 78a.56(a) and the Solid Waste Management Act (35 PS 6018.301). The release of the fluid to the ditch, sediment trap, and outfall is a violation of the Clean Streams Law (35 PS 691.401). Due to the unknown volume and duration of this release, this site will be required to go through the Act 2 process.

Violation ID: 8164677
Permit API: 125-22304
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Somerset Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/06/2023
Comments: On November 6 2023, the Department conducted an inspection of the Cole 1 OG Well in response to an OGI referral of the production tank leaking what appeared to be production fluid. At the time of inspection, the well appeared to drilled and equipped for production. The well tag was present on the well head. During the inspection, it appeared the production tank had previously been leaking at a valve near the bottom of the tank, but did not appear to be actively leaking. Distressed vegetation was observed in an approximate 3 foot radius around the tank. Directly below the valve, there appeared to be an excess amount of fluid along with a thick oil based matter. A background conductivity reading was taken and was 0.15 mS. Conductivity readings were taken in the soil in the area of the spill. The readings were elevated in comparison to the background reading with readings of 0.25mS, 0.45mS, 0.39mS, and 0.46mS. Elevated readings were detected in about a 3 foot radius around the production tank. Prior to leaving the location, the Department contacted KPI Representative Joel Greco to inform him of the release. Mr. Greco indicated that they had already replaced the faulty valve, and estimated the spill was roughly 15 barrels of production fluids and impacted the ground roughly 8 inches in depth. He stated remediation was scheduled to begin on 11/8/2023. I recommended that the Operator take immediate action to remediate the area in accordance with the Department's current spill policy. The Department requests clarification as to what caused the release, the quantity and type of fluid released (including the oil based matter) and how this was determined, as well as how long it is believed the release was occurring. Please include the clarification information within the NOV response.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the failure to properly control production fluid (and/or other fluids) resulting in a release to the ground, as well as failure to report a release.

Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-04-13
Comments: Due to COVID-19 restrictions, an admin inspection is being conducted. This inspection is being conducted in response to a report submitted by the operator on 4/11/2020 at approximately 0900 hours via the DEP hotline that a spill of approximately 20 gallons occurred on the Prentice Well Pad located in Forward Township, Allegheny County. According to the operator, at approximately 0800 hours on 4/11/2020, the dump line on a portable production tank malfunctioned and allowed production fluid to spray out in the direction of the Production Tanks. The inoperable section was reportedly fixed, and the operator remediated the impacted area by removing visually impacted material. The operator reported that no WOTC were threatened or impacted by this release. The Department requests a copy of the operators on-site PPC plan and Safety Data Sheets for the site be submitted to the Department electronically no later than 24 hours after receipt of this inspection. The Department requests the monthly inspection reports for all tanks on the site that store brine or other production fluids from 1/1/2020 to receipt of this inspection by 4/17/2020. The Department requested the waste manifest for the clean up as soon as it becomes available. Based on this inspection, violations are being noted as immediately corrected. Pending the operator's response, and further investigation, more violations may be issued.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/11/2023 to STONEHAVEN ENERGY MGT CO LLC in Howe Twp, Forest county. SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STONEHAVEN ENERGY MGT CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/11/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 995084
Permit API: 053-29526
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/11/2023
Comments: This conventional well is equipped with rods and tubing. The pump jack has been removed from the well, the annulus of the well remains connected to a gathering line. There was no activity onsite during this inspection. The well is not equipped with a well tag, nor is there a site ID sign posted at the location.A tank battery containing four steel tanks and two poly tanks inside of an earthen containment is located approximately 200 feet east of this well. There are indications that production fluids (primarily brine) have repeatedly been released onto the gravel inside of this containment. The soil is stained and specific conductance of the soil is elevated at the western edge where fluid from the tanks appears to have been released, and at the eastern edge of the containment where fluids appear to have been released from a pipeline riser/blow off).Vegetation is absent and deer tracks are very dense on the surface outside of the west/northwest extent of the containment, as it appears the released fluids have migrated through the earthen walls at the natural contour onto which the gravel and earthen wells were constructed. Stained soil and elevated specific conductance continue westward into a roadside ditch of Forest Road 219 until the ditch reaches a cross culvert approximately 300 feet away.Multiple sections of the Warrant 2980 lease roads beyond this well to the vicinity of well #'s 053-29931, 053-29930, 053-29944, 053-29955 and 053-29945 have not been sufficiently maintained. BMPs (ditches and cross culverts) that are installed along these roads are not functioning properly, as a result, accelerated erosion is occurring over various stretches of the road surface. These E and S concerns are considered part of E and S violations that are documented in the 5/11/23 inspection report for 053-29816 (Warrant 2980 #45).It is requested that documentation of production water disposal from this lease be provided to the Department. Please see the attached Notice of Violation regarding requested information pertaining to the cause of the release and intentions to remediate the contaminated material within and outside of the tank battery.
